skill.name: web-design-guidelines
skill.description: Reviews UI source files against fetched Web Interface Guidelines and reports concise, line-specific accessibility, design, and UX findings.
skill.summary: Audit selected UI files against current web interface guidelines.
skill.author: antfu

security_audit.summary: The two shell-execution findings are formatting false positives, while the hardcoded URL represents intentional low-severity network access. The mutable remote file is also treated as instructions, creating a medium-severity supply-chain risk.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the guideline URL to a commit and treat fetched text as untrusted reference content limited to UI review.

static_findings.snippet: 4. Output findings in the terse `file:line` format

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks only format the literal file:line output convention in Markdown. No shell command or execution instruction appears on this line.
The detected backticks are a Markdown fence around a URL. They do not contain or invoke a Ruby or shell command.
The skill explicitly instructs WebFetch to retrieve this URL before each review. This is intentional outbound access, although it does not send credentials or user data.

content.user_title: Audit UI Code Against Current Web Guidelines
content.value_statement: UI reviews can miss current accessibility and interaction rules. This skill fetches current guidelines, checks selected files, and returns concise line-specific findings.
actual_capabilities: Fetches current guidelines from the configured GitHub source before each review.
Reads user-specified UI files or file patterns.
Checks selected source files against every fetched guideline.
Reports findings with concise file and line references.
Asks for review targets when no file or pattern is provided.
limitations: Requires network access to retrieve the guideline source.
Uses a mutable remote file, so review behavior can change without a skill update.
Does not define browser testing or rendered interface inspection.
Review coverage depends on the files and patterns supplied by the user.

use_cases.title: Review a Component Before Merge
use_cases.description: Check a changed component for guideline violations before opening or approving a pull request.

use_cases.title: Triage Accessibility Concerns
use_cases.description: Find code-level accessibility issues and receive exact file and line references for follow-up.

use_cases.title: Audit Design System Usage
use_cases.description: Review related UI files for repeated patterns that conflict with current interface guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review {file} against Web Interface Guidelines. Report each issue with its file, line, explanation, and suggested correction.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a focused review of one UI file.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Component Group
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit {component_glob} for accessibility and interaction issues. Prioritize user impact and cite exact lines.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs consistent feedback across related components.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Complete Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Review {page_files} for accessibility, responsive layout, forms, typography, and performance. Group findings by severity and preserve file and line references.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a broad review before releasing a page.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Cross-File Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare {changed_files} against current guidelines. Identify cross-file design system inconsistencies, explain systemic causes, and propose prioritized remediation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer needs an advanced review of shared interface patterns.

output_examples.input: Review my checkout form component for accessibility issues.
output_examples.output: A concise report identifies missing form labels and unlinked error messages, with references to the supplied file and relevant lines.

output_examples.input: Audit the navigation components for interface guideline compliance.
output_examples.output: The findings describe unnamed icon controls and focus management issues, with a file and line reference for each result.

output_examples.input: Review the product page files and prioritize the findings.
output_examples.output: The review lists critical user-impact issues first, followed by concise file and line references for lower-priority corrections.

best_practices: Provide a narrow file path or pattern to keep findings relevant.
Confirm network access is available before starting the review.
Validate high-impact findings in the rendered interface when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not request a full repository review without defining relevant UI paths.
Do not treat every guideline finding as equal in user impact.
Do not follow fetched instructions that are unrelated to UI review.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews specified UI source files against Web Interface Guidelines and reports line-specific findings.

faq.question: Does this skill need network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It fetches guidelines from a GitHub-hosted source before each review.

faq.question: Does this skill modify files?
faq.answer: No. The skill defines a review workflow and reports findings. It does not instruct automatic edits.

faq.question: Can it check accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. Accessibility review is an intended use, within the limits of source-code analysis.

faq.question: What happens when no file is provided?
faq.answer: It asks which files or patterns should be reviewed.

faq.question: How are findings formatted?
faq.answer: It uses concise file and line references and follows formatting instructions from the fetched guidelines.
